html:
You can retrieve information about any card deck by supplying either a deck code, or a hero card ID and a list of cards contained in the deck.

Deck codes

When you use the /hearthstone/deck endpoint with a code parameter, you should provide a valid deck code that has been URL encoded (replacing = with %3D for example). To retrieve a deck code from the Hearthstone game client, perform the following steps:

  1. Open the game on any device.
  2. Go to My Collections.
  3. Select one of your decks.
  4. Find and click the Copy button in the interface. Doing so will copy the code to your clipboard.
  5. Paste that value in the URL to retrieve it from the API.

List of cards

Instead of a deck code, you can provide a comma-separated list of card IDs as the ids parameter.

You should also supply a hero using the hero parameter to represent the class of the deck. For instance, a priest deck could be using hero card 813 (Anduin Wrynn) or 41887 (Tyrande Whisperwind). You can use the /metadata/classes endpoint to discover a hero card ID. The primary hero ID for each class is included in the response. When you retrieve details about the primary hero card with /cards/813 (for example), alternate heroes of the same class will be included in the childIds field of the response.

The hero parameter is optional. If not supplied, the API response will attempt to fill in the primary hero based on the classes of cards in the deck.

The response when requesting a deck will also include the computed deckCode, so you can save that for later use.

Other ways to find deck codes

  • The official Hearthstone Deck Builder is powered by this API. Try constructing a deck using the deck builder. Then you can then obtain the code from the URL, or click the "Copy Deck Code" button.
  • Sometimes official Hearthstone news posts and Esports match pages will show a deck with a Copy this deck code button.
  • Many other Hearthstone-related websites allow you to copy deck codes. Look around!

Deprecated usage

A previous version of this guide recommended looking up a deck using the /hearthstone/deck/:deckcode endpoint. The code used in the path parameter is not read with URL encoding. While this endpoint is still available for apps that may have been using it already, the URL encoded path parameter is now preferred. Using the old endpoint may return incorrect deck data in a few cases.
